64.literal: I'm gonna report back to the boss properly, you know.
64.official: You pull some slacker bullshit on me, you can bet your leisure-suited ass the boss is gonna hear about it.

65.literal: The squatter's got the yakuza backing him, right?
65.official: But this squatter guy's got the yakuza backing him, right?

66.literal: That's where I get to show what I can do.
66.official: Guess that depends on how good I am.

67.literal: This is what they call business etiquette.
67.official: We're back to business etiquette 101, kid.

68.literal: Maybe it's on a side street branching off Tenkaichi Street.
68.official: (Might be tucked away on one of the smaller streets off Tenkaichi.)

69.literal: Heh, that was a pretty rough negotiation.

70.literal: In this work, knowing which approach to use when is what matters.
70.official: There's a time and a place for everything.

72.literal: First we've got to drag out the real party we're negotiating with.
72.official: Step one is to bring them to the table.

73.literal: You're slow, Kiryu-kun. They're our real negotiating partners, obviously.
73.official: Not the sharpest knife, are you, Kiryu-kun? Say hello to our real negotiation partners.

74.literal: It means we got a reaction right away.

75.literal: ...I heard you're here on Yamanoi-san's behalf.
75.official: I heard you're here on Yamanoi-san's behalf.

76.literal: I see. ...And as your brokerage fee for that,
76.official: And how much are you asking for the pleasure of your negotiating services?

77.literal: If you resell that building, you'll make a hundred million in profit, right?
77.official: Sell a building that size, you're looking at 100 million yen in profit.

78.literal: So this was how the script went?
78.official: Oda... was this your plan from the start?

79.literal: Were there too many of them for you?
79.official: Why, is this too overwhelming for a rookie's first day on the job?

80.literal: Heh, and how much is this fee for your trouble?
80.official: Heh, and just how much will that run us?

81.literal: Three million. That's ten million in total!
81.official: Three mil. That brings us to ten million yen!

82.literal: It'll be too late to regret making enemies of us...
82.official: Too late to unfuck yourselves now. You made the wrong enemies.

83.official: We had to bump into a Dojima man's goons. That certainly makes things messier.

84.literal: Your backing is as you see, Tsuji-san.
84.official: Your backup is, well, you can see for yourself.

85.official: N-No, sir! Wouldn't dream of it!

86.literal: It's the way I was taught.
86.official: Everything I know, I learned from the boss.

87.literal: ...Well, I guess that's pretty good for a first job.
87.official: Not bad, for your first job.

89.literal: You're more generous than I expected.

90.literal: That old man bowling with his own ball is
90.official: He's a hardcore bowler. Got his own ball, the whole shebang.

91.literal: his daily routine. You should be able to find him if you go to Mach Bowl.
91.official: I'd head to Mach Bowl. You'll probably find him there.

92.literal: I'll walk around for a bit, then head back to the office.
92.official: I should go for a stroll and then check back in later.

93.literal: I just can't believe you're in your right mind. You left the family and
93.official: Way I see it, you musta lost your goddamn mind.

94.literal: If you want to rush to your death, that's your business, but
94.official: You got a death wish, that's on you.

96.literal: I've got no intention of apologizing to you guys.
96.official: I have no intention of apologizing to you.

97.literal: But in exchange, this is the final line.
97.official: 'cause this is the last line in the sand.

98.literal: Boss Awano has gone out of his way to come out here himself, right nearby.
98.official: Lieutenant Awano's right upstairs. Came out here in person.

100.literal: Yeah. You mean Nishikiyama, and that buddy of yours from Tachibana Real Estate?
100.official: Right, Nishikiyama and that Tachibana Real Estate buddy of yours?

102.literal: Because I heard you were mixed up with Tachibana Real Estate.
102.official: Only reason I dragged my ass out here on a job like this is 'cause I heard you were wrapped up with Tachibana now.

103.literal: Heh, you're bad at covering things up.
103.official: Heh, you're pretty shit at hiding things.

104.literal: Even so, he must have at least got hold of a lead.
104.official: But he's at least got a clue by now.

105.literal: The quickest way to meet him is to have you act as go-between.
105.official: Having you arrange it seems like the quickest route to the guy.

106.literal: From every organization under the Dojima Family.
106.official: Every crew under the Dojima Family'd be gunnin' for you.

107.literal: Even if you run off and hide in prison, it won't do you any good.
107.official: Now don't think you could run away to prison.

108.literal: We'll hound you until you die.
108.official: We'd stay on your ass till you drew your last breath, wherever you hide.

109.literal: And don't think you'll get to die easy.
109.official: And don't think for a damn second it'd be a quick death.

110.literal: At this rate, he'll get caught in the fallout from you.
110.official: You keep this up, he's collateral damage. Your damage.

111.literal: Every last bit of info on the "Empty Lot"
111.official: Beat every bit of intel he's got on the Empty Lot outta him.

112.literal: I'm just gonna make him spit it out.
112.official: Beat every bit of intel he's got on the Empty Lot outta him. That's all.

113.literal: After that, I'll kindly ask the outsider to make his exit.

114.literal: If I don't get an answer... the "hunt" begins.
114.official: If I don't hear from you... the hunt's on.

115.literal: And the prey, naturally, will be your head.
115.official: We'll be coming for your head, to add to the collection.

117.literal: Where are you planning to seat the client when he gets here?
117.official: What's the client going to do, plop down on the tabletop?

118.literal: Hey, you're not seriously thinking of sitting in the seat of honor, are you?
118.official: C'mon, you're not really going to sit at the head, are you?

119.literal: Knowing it means nothing if you can't put it into practice.
119.official: Fat lot of good that does, if you can't act on it.

121.literal: The yakuza put just as much weight on hierarchy.
121.official: The business world's no different from the yakuza as far as strict hierarchy goes.

122.literal: Because you wouldn't get off with just a beating.
122.official: Sit down without thinking of your proper place and you could get a lot worse than decked.

124.literal: The yakuza are way stricter about manners, you know?
124.official: The yakuza are way more uptight about protocol.

125.literal: The higher up someone is, the better they know how to conduct themselves.
125.official: The higher up the ranks, the more formal those guys know how to act.

126.literal: Um, sir, at this establishment, beer is...
126.official: Er, I'm sorry sir, we don't serve beer here...

127.literal: Ah, sorry about the hard-to-get joke!
127.official: Sorry, my buddy here's jokes are so hard to get.
